abstract: This paper shows that, in measurement-based quantum computation, it is possible to write any quantum oracle implementing a classical function in constant depth. The result is shown through the equivalence between MBQC and the circuit model where arbitrary rotations along $Z$ axis and unbounded fan-outs are elementary operations. A corollary of this result is that disjunction can be implemented exactly in constant-depth, answering an open question of Høyer and Špalek.

specification.problem: Show that in measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) any quantum oracle implementing a classical function can be written in constant depth, via equivalence between MBQC and a circuit model with arbitrary Z-axis rotations and unbounded fan-outs as elementary operations; as a corollary, disjunction (OR) is implementable exactly in constant depth.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level problem statement and a small finite-instance sketch of the oracle and constant-depth claim; the actual construction, depth constants and MBQC pattern are not in the abstract and are not reconstructed.

specification.initial_state: Assumed: |x>|b>|0...0> for a computational-basis input; general superposition inputs follow by linearity.

steps.description: Use the circuit-model equivalent of MBQC with elementary gates being arbitrary Z rotations R_Z(theta) and unbounded fan-out (plus standard Hadamard/Clifford basis changes, assumed).

Assumed sketch: write f as a phase/parity-based expansion, fan out the x bits in one layer, apply parallel Z rotations to parity registers in one layer, then uncompute fan-out so total depth is independent of n. Exact construction is not in the abstract.
Conjugate the target qubit with Hadamards to turn the phase oracle into the bit-flip oracle O_f. For f=OR, this gives the exact constant-depth disjunction oracle stated as a corollary.

specification.measurement: Assumed: in the circuit picture, measure the x and b registers in the computational basis to read x and b XOR f(x); ancillas are uncomputed or measured and discarded. In the MBQC realization, the single-qubit measurement angles and adaptive corrections come from the equivalence and are not given in the abstract.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Assumed: none beyond reading the output bit b XOR f(x) (XOR with known b). Any MBQC Pauli-frame byproduct corrections are computed classically as parities of earlier outcomes; details unspecified.
